purpose: Define which contextual English expressions enter candidate-independent VPC/VID discovery before source sampling, annotation training, or model development.

project_scope.unit: One context-indexed occurrence in a document admitted by the later benchmark source and sampling protocol.
project_scope.inference_boundary: Results apply only to the frozen benchmark source frame and its prespecified strata; this contract alone does not define a register, period, national variety, or population distribution.
project_scope.source_frame_dependency: IR-110 fixes lawful source access and IR-121 fixes the document population and target-blind priority queues. Source rows and final per-stratum counts remain unavailable until the frozen dump is acquired and IR-127 fixes precision-based allocation.

primary_reference.reason: The executable contract and STREUSLE 5.0 projection use the PARSEME 1.2 VPC.full, VPC.semi, and VID labels.

taxonomy.current_reference_note: PARSEME 2.0 renames VPC to IVPC. The project retains the 1.2 labels for compatibility and must state the correspondence rather than silently mixing versions.

mapping.operational_boundary: A lexicalized head verb and dependent particle form a fully non-compositional unit; removing the particle cannot refer to the same event or state in context.
A lexicalized head verb and dependent particle form a partly non-compositional unit in which the particle adds a partly predictable non-spatial meaning and has a spatial literal counterpart.
A lexicalized verb and at least one lexicalized dependent satisfy the PARSEME VID lexical and morphosyntactic fixedness tests and are not better assigned to an excluded category.

candidate_independent_discovery.first_pass: Read every sentence in each sampled document in source order without consulting a target list, dictionary inventory, model suggestion, or downstream outcome. Mark every plausible lexicalized verb-plus-dependent combination that could instantiate an in-scope category.
candidate_independent_discovery.candidate_policy: Discovery is deliberately broader than the gold population. Literal counterparts, accidental sequences, particle/preposition ambiguities, and uncertain category cases remain visible as candidates until confirmed, rejected, or left unresolved.
candidate_independent_discovery.assisted_pass: A later list, rule, or model pass may add missed candidates only with distinct candidate-source provenance. It cannot erase first-pass decisions or create gold by itself.
candidate_independent_discovery.document_completion: A document is discovery-complete only after every sentence has received the candidate-independent pass, including sentences with no marked candidate.

required: The lexical head is a verb occurrence in English context.
The candidate has at least two lexicalized member tokens in document order.
The occurrence can be evaluated in its complete admitted document context.
The contextual combination can be assigned VPC.full, VPC.semi, or VID under the frozen taxonomy, or is retained as unresolved pending the guide decision tree.

terminal_states.confirmed: The contextual occurrence satisfies one in-scope category.
terminal_states.rejected: The surface sequence is compositional, accidental, outside the taxonomy, or otherwise not an in-scope occurrence.
terminal_states.unresolved: The evidence or rule is insufficient; do not force a category or convert absence of decision into rejection.

form_and_span_rules.canonical_form: Use the lowercase conventional citation form, lemmatizing the verbal head and preserving function words needed to identify the expression. It is a review label, is not derived mechanically from member IDs, and is not a stable sense or type identifier.
form_and_span_rules.inflection: Finite, non-finite, tense, aspect, agreement, and ordinary orthographic inflection of the verbal member are eligible. Auxiliaries are not members unless separately lexicalized by the expression.
form_and_span_rules.particle_separation: Continuous and separated VPC realizations are eligible. Every non-member token strictly between the first and last member is a gap.
form_and_span_rules.pronoun_insertion: An intervening pronoun or full noun-phrase object is a gap, not an MWE member, unless the pronoun is itself lexically fixed by the expression.
form_and_span_rules.overlap: Overlapping and nested candidates are recorded independently. A token may belong to more than one occurrence; later density summaries count the member-token union once.
form_and_span_rules.literal_use: A literal or accidental use of a known surface form remains a candidate negative and is rejected if it does not instantiate an in-scope VPC/VID. Occurrence category and the separate idiomaticity field must not be collapsed.
form_and_span_rules.ambiguity: If particle/preposition status, membership, or category cannot be resolved under the guide, preserve the candidate as unresolved rather than choosing the more familiar form.

out_of_scope.rule: Retain only if a separate in-scope VPC/VID analysis also applies; otherwise record the exclusion without broadening the first-paper taxonomy.
Exclude from the core population and treat any later inclusion as a new scope version.

examples: spelled-together or hyphenated forms with no second token
out_of_scope.rule: Exclude because the primary unit requires at least two lexicalized member tokens.

examples: a misspelled particle or fixed dependent
out_of_scope.rule: Do not silently correct or include in the core population. Preserve as a separately coded scope-extension candidate if learner-language robustness is later authorized.
Downstream relevance cannot determine core population membership or document sampling.

minimum_examples.point: Inflection and a separated full noun-phrase object remain eligible.
A partly predictable non-spatial completion particle is not collapsed with VPC.full.

minimum_examples.text: After months of secrecy, he spilled the beans.
minimum_examples.point: A verb with lexically fixed dependents is considered under the VID tests.

minimum_examples.text: He spilled the beans onto the floor.
minimum_examples.point: A literal counterpart is surfaced for rejection; surface identity does not create a VID occurrence.
A spatial prepositional use is a negative or unresolved candidate, not an automatic VPC.

shared: Project VPC.full, VPC.semi, and VID map exactly to STREUSLE strong labels V.VPC.full, V.VPC.semi, and V.VID for evaluation.
Member tokens remain in source order and discontinuity is determined from gaps between members.
different: The project discovery population includes rejected and unresolved candidates; the committed STREUSLE projection contains only annotated strong target occurrences.
STREUSLE supersenses are not project fine-grained contextual senses.
The project records idiomaticity, inventory coverage, assignment, ambiguity, abstention, and out-of-inventory separately; the STREUSLE projection does not supply those gold labels.
The exposed STREUSLE test projection is development evidence, not the new sealed test or a population sample of all English.

change_rule: Any change to included categories, minimum member count, literal-use handling, spelling policy, or category mapping is breaking and requires a new contract version plus a decision-log record.
